expectations.text: Applies the pooling compatibility test before any portfolio: same conversion event, comparable margins, same target
expectations.evidence: The transcript argues incompatibility via 'different buyer intents at different funnel depths with different economics' but never frames the test as same conversion event / comparable margins / same target — no mention of conversion-event sameness at all.

expectations.text: Rejects pooling the brand campaign with prospecting campaigns
expectations.evidence: "Pooling a brand line with prospecting is the specific case this kind of policy exists to catch."

expectations.text: Explains that pooled spend migrates on blended rather than per-campaign returns, distorting allocation when economics differ
expectations.evidence: "Pooling migrates spend toward whichever campaign's economics dominate the blended signal (almost always branded), silently starving or mispricing the other two."

expectations.text: Acknowledges pooling legitimately helps thin campaigns clear signal floors when the pooled goals are genuinely compatible
expectations.evidence: Pooling is only framed negatively as "the agency's way to synthetically clear that floor"; the transcript never states pooling can be a legitimate fix when campaigns are genuinely compatible — it instead offers 'volume-appropriate archetype' or 'structural consolidation' as the alternatives.

expectations.text: Names the diagnostic for pooling gone wrong: blended target looks fine while per-campaign returns diverge, so incompatible campaigns get split out
expectations.evidence: No diagnostic of this kind appears anywhere in the transcript; the rejection is argued a priori from funnel-depth/economics differences, not via a blended-vs-per-campaign divergence check.

expectations.text: Suggests consolidation as the alternative fix for structurally thin campaigns
expectations.evidence: "or genuine structural consolidation if the segmentation is redundant — not blending unlike economics under one shared target."

expectations.text: States that LinkedIn does not offer value-based / return-goal bidding
expectations.evidence: The transcript treats LinkedIn value-based bidding as an available archetype merely lacking a data signal: "value-based bidding optimizes toward deal value. With no Salesforce-to-LinkedIn pipe, there's no value signal to optimize toward — the archetype has nothing to run on yet." It never claims LinkedIn lacks the capability itself.

expectations.text: Treats bidding capabilities as observed per platform rather than assuming feature parity across platforms
expectations.evidence: The two platforms are treated identically under one blanket rule ("Same gate, no exception") with no per-platform capability check distinguishing Google's and LinkedIn's actual bidding feature sets.

expectations.text: Notes Google's return-goal (Target ROAS) carries a documented minimum for Search (15 conversions in the past 30 days) with an as-of or re-verify caveat
expectations.evidence: "Target ROAS on Search documents a 15-conversions/30-days minimum." is stated, but no as-of date or re-verify caveat (e.g. 'confirm current threshold') accompanies it.

expectations.text: Blocks any return-goal recommendation until real differentiated values actually flow back, since nothing flows from the CRM yet
expectations.evidence: "no conversion values flow from Salesforce to Google or LinkedIn today... A Target ROAS or value-based strategy needs real deal values to optimize against... That's not a target-setting problem, it's a measurement problem, and it blocks both asks regardless of campaign size."

expectations.text: Requires legal/privacy/consent review before Salesforce deal values are sent to any platform
expectations.evidence: "sending deal values to Google and LinkedIn is a data-sharing decision, not just a technical one — expect a consent/data-processing review before that pipe goes live, and treat that review as part of the project, not an afterthought once the integration is built."

expectations.text: Runs the value-integrity check (values differentiated, net of refunds/rejects, timely relative to lag) as a prerequisite
expectations.evidence: "Build the CRM-to-platform value passback: differentiated deal values (not one flat number), net of lost/disqualified deals, timely enough relative to your sales cycle to matter to the bidder."

expectations.text: Notes the 9-14 conversion/month campaigns clear no documented return-goal minimum on their own
expectations.evidence: "Competitor prospecting (14/mo) sits right under that bar; generic demand (9/mo) is well under it."

expectations.text: Applies the pooling compatibility test before any portfolio: same conversion event, comparable margins, same target
expectations.evidence: "Branded (120 conv/mo) has fundamentally different economics than the other two: near-100% purchase intent, low CPC, high win-rate. Competitor and generic campaigns are cold-intent, higher CPC, lower win-rate." — the transcript checks economics/intent compatibility before endorsing pooling.

expectations.text: Rejects pooling the brand campaign with prospecting campaigns
expectations.evidence: "Portfolio Target ROAS across branded + competitor + generic — reject" and "Split branded out of any pooled strategy permanently"

expectations.text: Explains that pooled spend migrates on blended rather than per-campaign returns, distorting allocation when economics differ
expectations.evidence: "the portfolio's pacing and bid signal gets set by branded's cheap, easy conversions, then gets applied to prospecting traffic that behaves nothing like it. That's a way to overpay on competitor/generic"

expectations.text: Acknowledges pooling legitimately helps thin campaigns clear signal floors when the pooled goals are genuinely compatible
expectations.evidence: "If there's a legitimate portfolio case, it's competitor + generic together (similar funnel stage, similar intent), once combined volume and value data support it"

expectations.text: Names the diagnostic for pooling gone wrong: blended target looks fine while per-campaign returns diverge, so incompatible campaigns get split out
expectations.evidence: The transcript states the problem in advance (branded will dominate signal) but never describes a diagnostic for detecting divergence after the fact (e.g., monitoring per-campaign performance against a healthy-looking blended average) as a way to catch pooling going wrong and trigger a split.

expectations.text: Suggests consolidation as the alternative fix for structurally thin campaigns
expectations.evidence: The transcript only mentions Google's 30-conversion guidance and notes competitor/generic don't clear it, but does not propose consolidating campaigns (e.g., merging ad groups/campaigns) as a fix for thin volume — the only volume-related fix offered is a competitor+generic portfolio, not campaign consolidation itself.

expectations.text: States that LinkedIn does not offer value-based / return-goal bidding

expectations.text: Treats bidding capabilities as observed per platform rather than assuming feature parity across platforms
expectations.evidence: The transcript assumes LinkedIn has an equivalent value-based bidding mechanism ("mirroring value-based bidding") and treats it as implementable once data flows, rather than verifying/distinguishing platform capability differences.

expectations.text: Notes Google's return-goal (Target ROAS) carries a documented minimum for Search (15 conversions in the past 30 days) with an as-of or re-verify caveat
expectations.evidence: The transcript cites "~30 conversions/30 days" as "Google's own guidance" without an as-of/re-verify caveat, and this figure does not match the specific 15-conversion Target ROAS Search minimum the rubric expects.

expectations.text: Requires legal/privacy/consent review before Salesforce deal values are sent to any platform
